eat: 방어회, raw slices with soy sauce and wasabi
김 wrap, raw slices in dried seaweed
blurb: A big, fatty yellowtail eaten raw in thick slices. It is caught all year, but demand opens in November and the fat peaks Dec-Feb. Seafood expert Kim Ji-min says February often beats December, and the main fishing ground is moving from Jeju to the East Coast.
caveat: A 10 kg+ fish sold for 371,000 won in Nov 2025, against 270,000 won a year earlier. Goseong's catch fell from 4,060 t in 2022 to 2,202 t in 2024.

eat: 알 and 이리, roe and milt in soup

closures.note: Press reports a January closure, so check current notices

blurb: A big cold-water cod, stewed with its roe and milt. It fills out from mid November and peaks from late December to January. The fish stay in Jinhae Bay Dec-Feb and head north in March.
caveat: A one-month January closure cuts into the peak, according to the newspaper Seoul Shinmun. Another article puts the start at Jan 15, so check current fisheries ministry notices.

blurb: Clear pufferfish soup (bokguk) is the classic winter meal, a Busan and Masan habit. The fish is caught all year but eaten Nov-Mar. Chambok, kkachibok and milbok are different types, and all sell under the name bogeo.
A soft, watery winter fish (standard name kkomchi) cooked in a clear soup and sold as a hangover cure. Peak is Dec-Mar. Fishing at Chudo runs about three months from Dongji, the winter solstice.
caveat: Tongyeong tradition points to January as the best month.

blurb: Monkfish turns up steamed, braised and in soup, and peaks Dec-Feb. Sources disagree on when the season opens.
caveat: One account starts it at Ipdong, the start of winter in early November. Elle magazine says February.

eat: Wrapped in 생미역 (fresh seaweed) with 초장
Wrapped in 쌈 or plain 돌김
festivals: Guryongpo Gwamegi Culture Center weekend tastings, Nov-Dec 2026
blurb: Fish dried in sea wind, mostly saury now and formerly herring. Split fish dry from about November, and whole fish only from December. A warm October in 2025 pushed drying back to early and mid November.

festivals: Sokcho festival for 양미리 and 도루묵 (16th), Nov 7-16, 2025
blurb: A sandfish that runs to spawn in early winter, Nov-Dec, and is eaten for its roe, grilled or braised. Sokcho and Jumunjin are the main ports.

festivals: Sokcho festival for 양미리 and 도루묵 (16th), Nov 7-16, 2025
blurb: A small winter fish dried on racks in Goseong, according to one photo report. The Nov-Dec window rests on festival timing alone, and no recipe is sourced.

closures.note: Domestic catch banned all year since 2019

blurb: Pollock has a different name at each stage: saengtae fresh, dongtae frozen, kodari half-dried and nogari juvenile. Domestic catch has been banned all year since 2019, so the fresh domestic season is effectively gone. Raw fish is mostly Russian.
caveat: The Dec-Jan window rests on a single list on Namuwiki. Treat it as a lead.

blurb: Eaten salt-grilled or raw, Spanish mackerel runs Oct-Feb and is fattest in winter. The fisheries ministry says it starts in November. Spring and summer catch is rising.
caveat: The West Sea closure moved from May to Apr 10-May 10, which puts spring fish in shops.

blurb: A herring that comes in winter to early spring and spawns Dec-Apr. No source names months, so the window here is an estimate. It was the original fish for gwamegi, the wind-dried fish.

closures.note: Report says May, no exact dates

blurb: A sea bream eaten raw or in spicy stew. Wild fish are a Nov-Dec pick. Shops sell it through April as a last chance before the May closure, but the national fisheries institute rates spring fish poor.
Mullet is eaten raw and counts as a Dec-Jan winter fish in press and festival accounts. The season is disputed.
caveat: One wiki says Feb-Apr, the fisheries ministry's monthly picks say Mar-Apr, and seafood expert Kim Ji-min calls one type, gasungeo, nearly done by February.

eat: 보리싹 and liver soup, early spring

closures.note: Appears to be, replacing an older May-Jun report

festivals: Yeongsanpo Hongeo Festival (영산포 홍어축제), May each year
blurb: Skate is eaten fermented, and that form is sold all year. Boiled with barley sprouts and liver, it makes a soup for early spring. The prime window of winter through March is an estimate.
caveat: A 2007 article gives a May-Jun closure, while a 2024 reading of the statute says Jun 1-Jul 15. Check current notices.

blurb: A lumpfish eaten in winter until early February, mostly as a roe stew with aged kimchi. Jumunjin and Daejin in Goseong are the ports. The start month is an estimate from the word winter.
An eelpout eaten half-dried and steamed in winter, until early February. East Coast ports from Samcheok to Goseong sell it. The start month is a guess from the word winter.
An East Coast fish nicknamed ugly, tied to winter by one source and sold at Jumunjin. No source gives a month or a recipe, only the names.
A Jeju fish that is fat in winter and thin after spawning. Kim Ji-min names February. It is mostly dried before grilling, and tilefish and seaweed soup is a Jeju birthday dish.
caveat: Only February is sourced. The wider winter-to-early-spring run is an estimate.

blurb: A striped beakperch eaten raw, picked by an insider for November flesh and fat. Wild and farmed juvenile fish both sell. Jeju and the south coast are the main grounds.
The juvenile form of the striped beakperch, eaten raw. An insider's pick says it is best in late Sep-Oct.
A Jeju fish eaten raw, picked by an insider for November. Wild catch there starts in autumn.
A grouper eaten raw, named from November by Kim Ji-min. No end month is given. Jeju, Busan and Samcheonpo are among the grounds.
A grouper eaten raw, listed from November in the same insider pick as jabari, the longtooth grouper. No end month is given.
A grilled fish picked by an insider for November. Gangwon and Yeosu are named as regions for this group of fish.
A grilled flounder picked by an insider for November. April market picks name it too, so spring is a second mention.
A flounder picked by an insider for November and eaten braised. Gangwon is a named region for the group.
A winter fish named in one insider guide as a cheaper stand-in for red sea bream. No month is given, and Jeju is the named place.
A winter fish named in one insider guide as a cheaper stand-in for red sea bream. No month is given.
A roughscale sole eaten raw or as a spicy raw salad. It is a single February market pick by Kim Ji-min.
A flounder eaten raw or as a spicy raw salad. It is a single February market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with jul-gajami and seongdae.
A gurnard eaten raw or as a spicy raw salad. It is a single February market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with jul-gajami and yong-gajami.

A halfbeak with a winter fishing season on the East and south coasts, from early winter to March, and the dates are an estimate. Raw and grilled dishes appear only in angler tables, so the food claim is thin.
Farmed trout is a festival draw more than an eating season. The Pyeongchang festival ran Jan 9-Feb 9 in 2026 and slipped a week for abnormal weather.
A masu salmon known for a huge winter ice-fishing festival in Hwacheon, and little as a food. The window follows the festival, which ran Jan 10-Feb 1 in 2026.

festivals: Inje Smelt Festival (인제빙어축제), cancelled 2026, last held 2023
blurb: A freshwater smelt tied to ice fishing on Soyang Lake. The Inje festival was cancelled in 2026, the third year running, because the ice failed. No source covers how it is eaten.

eat: 세꼬시, bone-in slices of young fish
blurb: A clear soup of marbled flounder and spring mugwort. The date comes from the mugwort, which is good only to early April. The fish itself is fattest in summer-autumn, and young fish give sekkosi, bone-in slices.
caveat: One YouTuber claims most spring fish is really farmed gang-dodari. Bones are too hard for raw slices by April.

blurb: Red sea bream is farmed widely, with wild fish from offshore. Kim Ji-min names April. It is eaten raw, sometimes with the skin scalded.
caveat: Sources disagree. One wiki says Nov-Mar, and the fisheries ministry's monthly picks are Feb, Jun and Aug.

blurb: A rockfish that Tongyeong eats all year, called a memory and not a fish by one Tongyeong columnist. One wiki puts the season at Mar-Apr, and winter and spring fish are firmest.
caveat: The Dec-May firmness window is an estimate. One YouTuber says nearly all fish sold as bollak are really yeolgi, a goldeye rockfish.

blurb: Atka mackerel is salted and grilled until the skin is crisp. It is caught all year, with the catch peaking Mar-May.

Gulbi, salted dried croaker, is made from roe-filled yellow croaker caught around Gogu, about Apr 20. The fisheries ministry's monthly picks fall in Sep and Nov. Drift gillnets are shut for much of spring and summer.
A small yellow croaker named in a single April market pick. No source gives an end month or a way of eating it.

eat: 쌈밥 찜, rice wrap and steamed
blurb: Fresh spring anchovy arrives Apr-May, when Daebyeon port in Gijang holds a festival. It is eaten raw, in a rice wrap or steamed. An official pick also names October.

windows.label: Caught late Mar to mid May

blurb: Tiny juvenile baedorachi, sold as baengeo. They are caught late March to mid May, but the raw window lasts only 2-3 weeks from early April. The fish dies fast, so it is eaten raw only near Janggohang port.
The true baengeo is nearly gone from Korea and spawns Apr-May. One wiki says it turns up only around Sinan and Jindo, where real baengeopo, dried sheets, is a rarity found Jun-Sep.
caveat: The Jun-Sep window rests on one wiki line. Most baengeopo on sale is made from silchi.

blurb: A tiny goby eaten live, with a short window from March to early May. Only Geoje's eastern district, Dongbu-myeon, sells it. It also goes into pancakes and soup.
A river anchovy that runs in Apr-May and is frozen the rest of the year. The Geum River and Buyeo are the home ground.

eat: 회 with 미나리, raw with water dropwort
blurb: A river pufferfish that runs up the Imjin River in spring and stays fresh for about one month. Wild fish cost about 200,000 won/kg in 2020.
caveat: The May 20 peak is an estimate.

blurb: A herring with a saying, sseogeodo junchi, meaning it is good even when spoiling. It vanishes after the season, hence the nickname siseo. At the Dano holiday it is made into soup and dumplings.
In Incheon and Ganghwa the fish sold under this name is really banji, an anchovy-family fish. Fat is gone by mid July. True baendaengi is a herring, sold dried as dipori.
Wild eel from Gochang, with a Mar-Jun window from one uncited Wikipedia line. It is a spring fish, not a Boknal one.
caveat: No source says how much farmed eel is sold under this name.

blurb: A farmed flounder sliced long and eaten raw. It is a single April market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with three other April picks, with no wider season given.
A small skate, steamed or put in soup. It is a single April market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with three other April picks, with no wider season given.
A small shark with no sourced recipe. It is a single April market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with three other April picks, with no wider season given.
A flounder-kin fish with no sourced recipe. It is a single April market pick by Kim Ji-min, grouped with three other April picks, with no wider season given.
A rockfish with no sourced month, usually sold as bollak. One YouTuber says nearly all fish sold as bollak are really yeolgi.

festivals: Sinan Mineo Festival, Imjado, early Aug each year

windows.label: Inshore from mid Jul to about Chuseok

blurb: A big croaker eaten for Boknal (복날), the three hottest days of summer, with a peak in early August at the top of Sambok. Offshore catch starts in June and the Imjado catch in mid July, running on to Chuseok. The Encyclopedia of Korean Culture already calls it in season at Soseo, a solar term.
caveat: Kim Ji-min says winter fish are nearly as good.

blurb: Farmed eel has no real season, but demand jumps in Jul-Aug for Boknal. The fisheries ministry's monthly picks range across Jan, Jul, Aug and Oct and state no season. The one sourced catch season is wild Gochang fish in spring.
caveat: One wiki gives May-Jun, and a 2009 Jinju list gave July grilling. Neither states a catch season.

blurb: A southern fish for bokdalim, eating to beat the summer heat, named alongside mineo (brown croaker). It runs Jun-Aug, and May-Sep overall. Some eat it in autumn in soup, when the bones harden.
Conger eel is sold all year. The prime window of summer to early autumn is an estimate. Tongyeong is the main distribution hub.

festivals: Island Pomfret Festival (섬 병어축제, 12th), Jido, Jun 12-13, 2026
blurb: A pomfret best in June before Haji, the summer solstice, with a May-Jul run. A box cost near 700,000 won in 2026. Large ones are called deokja.
Sea bass is eaten raw, often aged. Recent press calls it a summer fish, stable into November.
caveat: A classic text favours spring, so the summer window is an estimate.

blurb: A horse mackerel eaten raw or salt-grilled, with a Jeju soup too. Sources say summer, improving from April, with live fish still sold in September. All months are estimates, and spawning is Jun-Aug on the south coast.
A tonguefish that Yeosu mixes into a raw salad and puts on ancestral tables. The summer window rests on one Wikipedia sentence, so the months are an estimate.
Wild bluefin caught in Korean waters, eaten raw. One wiki says it comes in summer or early autumn, and the months here are an estimate. Quota, not season, sets supply.
caveat: The same wiki's older Apr-Jun entry and the March fisheries ministry picks look wrong for wild fish.

blurb: A small Jeju fish eaten whole in cold soup. The window follows the barley harvest, late May to early July, and Bomok in Seogwipo holds a festival in May.
A southern Jeju summer fish, eaten raw, grilled and in seaweed soup. No source gives a month.

eat: 된장 물회, cold soup with soybean paste
blurb: A rabbitfish from Jeju that is not farmed. Sources tie it to summer and say it sells into September, but give no month.

eat: 회 with 간, raw with liver
blurb: A filefish tied to summer and autumn, with no sourced month. Fans chase the liver, eaten with the raw fish.
A river fish that returns Mar-Jun, matures in Jul-Aug and spawns Sep-Oct. Hadong is the named place. The saying "chilpalwol eoneo gumdeut" points to July and August, when many fish die.
caveat: Closed seasons apply. The dates come from a video recap, so check current notices.

blurb: A freshwater fish eaten raw or in spicy stew. One wiki says domestic fish are plentiful Jun-Nov, and a dealer says they are hard to find mid Dec-mid Apr. That is trade lore for spotting domestic fish, not a food claim.
A Jeju grouper that old Jeju reckoning calls a summer fish, with no month given. Kim Ji-min prefers jabari, the longtooth grouper, in November.
A Jeju grouper eaten raw, called a summer fish by old Jeju reckoning, with no month given. Kim Ji-min prefers jabari, the longtooth grouper, in November.
Hagfish has no season and is eaten all year. Gijang grills it over a straw fire, and Jagalchi serves it over charcoal.

Gizzard shad is eaten bone-in raw or salt-grilled whole. It peaks early-mid September in the south and west, and late September-early October in Seoul. First shipments came mid July in 2026, and the smell of grilling shad is said to bring a runaway daughter-in-law home.
caveat: Some analysts see the peak sliding toward summer as waters warm. Sources dispute this.

blurb: Chub mackerel is a Sep-Nov fish, with farmed fish in winter. Catch fell to about 134,000 t in 2024.
caveat: No recipe source was found.

blurb: A spotted mackerel that is best from late August to October once it reaches 35 cm. No dish is sourced.
Hairtail is an autumn fish, and one wiki gives Jul-Oct. Jeju sells silver eungalchi and Mokpo sells a type called meokgalchi. Catch fell to about 44,000 t in 2024.
Saury is an Oct-Nov fish on one wiki list. It is mostly feedstock for gwamegi, the air-dried fish, now.
caveat: Thin sourcing. A single list gives the months.

blurb: Olive flounder is eaten raw. Wild fish run autumn to early winter, Sep-Dec by one wiki. Farmed fish stay even all year, and the national fisheries institute says farmed fish beat wild in spawning months. Jeju fish are best summer to autumn.
Korean rockfish is eaten raw. Wild fish run autumn to early winter, an estimate, and farmed fish even out the year. Large offshore fish come from Wando and Chuja.
A freshwater loach made into chueotang, a soup eaten as a boyang dish, meaning food for restoring strength. Farming removes the hard season. Official picks run Aug, Sep and Oct.
Chum salmon return up the Namdae River in October, an event more than a food. The festival is about viewing and catching, and no source covers how it is eaten.
A goby caught all year, with a Sep-Nov pick from Kim Ji-min. It is dried for soup, and braised or stewed.
A greenling of 30 cm or more, eaten raw, named in a September market pick as good to October. The start month is an estimate.
A white croaker named as a September market pick, eaten in stews and fried or grilled. The west coast of Jeonnam is the named ground.
A greater amberjack eaten raw. It is a September pick that works as a bridge to winter yellowtail (bangeo), and the months are an estimate.
A striped jack eaten raw, listed with jaetbangeo as a September bridge to winter yellowtail. The months are an estimate.
A flounder eaten bone-in and raw, or in cold soup, in summer and autumn. The West Sea is the named ground, and the months are an estimate.
A brown sole eaten bone-in and raw, or in cold soup, in summer and autumn. It is listed with dol-gajami, and the months are an estimate.
A Jeju fish named as a September market pick, eaten in a leaf wrap.

eat: 구이, grilled with seasoned soy sauce
blurb: One of the Yeosu 10 flavors, usually grilled with seasoned soy sauce. Two encyclopedias give it no season. One wiki calls it the top fish around Yeosu, with seodae (tonguefish) next.
River carp farmed year-round, mostly eaten in spicy summer stew. There is no real season, so it stays off the calendar.
A catfish eaten in spicy stew. It has no season, and its one official pick, in Aug 2025, called it among the most popular summer dishes. Restaurants away from rivers mostly use farmed fish.
A farmed carp eaten raw or in spicy stew, with no season. It was introduced in 1973, and output was about 1,700 t in 2025, fifth among inland fish.
Crucian carp is farmed, with demand only for summer spicy stew. There is no real season, so it stays off the calendar.
